notes: Verified: go build/vet clean; `go test ./internal/application ./internal/transport/httpapi -run OIDC` passes on HEAD. With oidc.go/auth_routes.go reverted to main, the httpapi test TestStandaloneOIDCFlowErrorAndLegacyRedirectURI fails (no incident recorded) and the application test package does not compile (oidcDiscover/RecordOIDCProviderError missing), so the new tests genuinely exercise the change. oidc_errors_test.go 'discovery' case now demands Count==2 + 'HTTP 502' + issuer URL in Detail, which could not pass before.

Success path of BeginOIDC/CompleteOIDC is untouched; only the discovery error path changed (oidc.NewProvider still called with the same ctx/issuer). Sanitisation holds: guidance strings are fixed literals, only the 3-digit HTTP status and the admin-configured issuer are interpolated; tests assert provider-controlled text does not leak into error, incident or logs.

internal/application/oidc.go:503 `errors.Is(err, syscall.ECONNREFUSED)` only matches on Unix; on Windows the dial error is WSAECONNREFUSED and falls through to the generic '*url.Error' branch ('인증 서버에 연결하지 못했습니다'). Degrades gracefully, not a defect.
internal/application/oidc.go:500 a DNS lookup that times out is a *net.DNSError and is classified as 'host not found' before the timeout branch is reached. Minor misclassification only.

internal/application/oidc.go:482 incident fingerprint is (component, severity, message) and the issuer is only in Detail, so discovery failures against two different issuers over time fold into one row with the latest issuer. Acceptable for dedupe semantics used elsewhere.
oidc_discovery_test.go 'connection_refused' relies on the closed httptest port not being reused before BeginOIDC dials it; theoretically flaky but practically fine.

No migrations, no external state, no unrelated refactors; docs/ADMIN_GUIDE.md update matches the implemented behaviour (silent-attempt login_required still not recorded, access_denied/login_required family as warning, unknown codes folded into generic row). Fully revertable.
